adjudication_records.issue_text: cook returns raw HTML verbatim for cook_methods[:raw_html] and PollFeed passes third-party RSS/Atom item content into TopicEmbed.import with no sanitization, stored as cooked and emitted via raw post.cooked — stored XSS from a malicious feed item (app/models/post.rb:131, app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces an explicit bypass of the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline: `Post#cook` now returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb). Feed-imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (TopicEmbed.import via PostCreator), and `Jobs::PollFeed` passes third-party feed item HTML (`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) into `TopicEmbed.import` without sanitizing dangerous tags/attributes (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, app/models/topic_embed.rb). The embed view then renders `post.cooked` using `raw` (`<%= raw post.cooked %>`), and specs confirm `post.cooked == post.raw` for raw_html. This is a verifiable stored XSS vector if a feed item contains script/event-handler HTML.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed 'imported from' footer interpolates url unescaped into <a href='#{url}'>, so a link containing a single quote breaks out of the attribute and injects HTML (app/models/topic_embed.rb:13)

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the code appends an HTML footer using string interpolation: `"#{url}"` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). The only validation on `url` is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent single quotes or other characters that can break out of the single-quoted href attribute. Because imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (bypassing the usual rendering/sanitization pipeline) and are later rendered with `raw post.cooked` in the embed view, a URL containing `'` can inject arbitrary HTML/JS, making this a real XSS risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb lacks render_views, so best.html.erb and loading.html.erb are never rendered by any spec and view errors ship green

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the only tests added for the new embed feature are controller specs (spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb). That spec file does not call `render_views`. In RSpec-Rails controller specs, views are not rendered/evaluated unless `render_views` is enabled, so the newly added templates (app/views/embed/best.html.erb, app/views/embed/loading.html.erb, and layout app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb) are not executed by these specs. There are also no separate view/request specs in the diff that would render them. As a result, template syntax/runtime errors could exist while the controller specs still pass.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:41-46 asserts TopicRetriever.expects(:new)/retriever.expects(:retrieve) but the controller calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...), so the test never verifies the job is enqueued with the right embed_url/user_id

adjudication.rationale: The finding is accurate: in `EmbedController#best`, when `topic_id` is nil it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and does not instantiate `TopicRetriever` or call `retrieve`. However, `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` (the example around lines 41-46) sets expectations on `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)`. With the controller code shown in the diff, that spec will fail and it also doesn’t verify the actual behavior (job enqueuing with correct args).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27-28 uses setnx followed by a separate expire (non-atomic); a crash between the calls leaves the retrieved:<url> key forever so that embed URL can never be retrieved again — should use SET key 1 NX EX 60

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb retrieved_recently? sets the throttle key with `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and only then calls `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These are two separate Redis commands; if the process crashes or loses connectivity after SETNX succeeds but before EXPIRE runs, the key will remain without a TTL. On subsequent calls, SETNX will return false and the method returns true (throttled), effectively preventing retrieval for that embed_url indefinitely until the key is manually deleted. Using an atomic `SET key value NX EX 60` (or a Lua script) avoids this failure mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:15-30 does a check-then-insert against a uniquely-indexed column, so concurrent PollFeed and RetrieveTopic imports of the same URL both create a topic and the second TopicEmbed.create! raises RecordNotUnique after the duplicate topic exists

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicEmbed.import` does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, proceeds to create a `Post`/`Topic` and then `TopicEmbed.create!(embed_url: url, ...)` inside a transaction. The migration adds a **unique index** on `topic_embeds.embed_url`. With concurrent import attempts for the same URL (e.g., `Jobs::PollFeed` calling `TopicEmbed.import` and `RetrieveTopic`/`TopicRetriever` calling `TopicEmbed.import_remote` -> `import`), both threads/processes can observe `embed.blank?` and create separate topics/posts; then the second `TopicEmbed.create!` will raise due to the unique index, leaving behind the extra topic/post created before the failure. There is no locking/upsert/`find_or_create_by`+retry to prevent this race in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 runs Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) synchronously inside the retrieve job — a full feed download plus import of every item per uncached embed URL, serializing N full feed polls under a burst of first-time embeds

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In lib/topic_retriever.rb `perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` directly (synchronously) whenever `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true and the embed hasn’t been found yet. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` then does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates `rss.items.each` importing every item. Because the throttle key in `retrieved_recently?` is per-embed URL (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), a burst of first-time embeds for different URLs can trigger multiple full feed downloads/import loops in separate RetrieveTopic executions, causing redundant work and potentially long-running sidekiq jobs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: open(url).read / open(feed_url) have no read timeout and no size limit, so a slow or huge remote response pins a Sidekiq worker indefinitely and buffers the whole body into memory (app/models/topic_embed.rb:48, app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces remote fetches via open-uri without any explicit bounds: `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `Jobs::PollFeed` and `open(url).read` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote`. Both will read the entire response body (and in the latter case explicitly slurp it into a single String) with no size limit, and there is no explicit read/open timeout configured on these calls. A slow/trickling or very large response can therefore tie up a Sidekiq worker for an unbounded duration and/or consume large memory while buffering the body.

adjudication_records.issue_text: open-uri follows redirects, so the SiteSetting.embeddable_host check in TopicRetriever#invalid_host? only validates the initial URL — an embeddable host that 302s to 169.254.169.254 or an internal service is fetched and imported (SSRF) (app/models/topic_embed.rb:48)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` only compares `URI(@embed_url).host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, i.e., it validates the *initial* URL host string. The actual fetch happens in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` via `open(url).read` (open-uri), which follows HTTP redirects by default. That means an embed URL on the allowed host (e.g. `http://allowed-host/redirect?...`) can redirect the server-side request to another host/IP (including `169.254.169.254` or internal services), and the redirected content would then be fetched and imported. There is no subsequent validation of the final destination after redirects in the diff, so this SSRF vector is present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 uses discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1, a substring test rather than an origin equality comparison, and never checks e.source === iframe.contentWindow
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. The candidate flags that using indexOf for origin validation is a substring check rather than strict origin equality, which is exactly the weakness described in the golden comment (e.g., a malicious domain containing the trusted domain could bypass it). It also adds an extra related concern about not checking e.source, but the core issue matches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: absolutize_urls' start_with?('/') test also matches protocol-relative URLs, rewriting //cdn.example.com/img.png to http://embedhost/cdn.example.com/img.png, while relative URLs without a leading slash (foo/bar.html, ../x) are left un-absolutized (app/models/topic_embed.rb)

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, links/images are rewritten only when href/src starts_with?('/'). This condition also matches protocol-relative URLs like "//cdn.example.com/img.png". The code then strips all leading slashes (href.sub(/^\/+/, '')) and prefixes the embed host, producing "http://<embedhost>/cdn.example.com/img.png", which is incorrect. Additionally, despite the method comment saying it converts relative URLs to absolute, it does not handle other relative forms like "foo/bar" or "../x" at all. Both behaviors are directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 uses contents << "..." which mutates the caller's string in place, so reuse or retry accumulates duplicate 'Imported from' footers, changing content_sha1 and triggering a spurious revision

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, `contents << "..."` destructively appends the footer to the caller-provided String. If the caller reuses the same `contents` String object (e.g., retries the import, caches and re-imports, or calls `import` twice with the same variable without reloading), the footer will be appended multiple times. Because `content_sha1` is computed after this mutation (`Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(contents)`), repeated calls can produce different SHA1s even when the underlying source content didn’t change, potentially triggering unnecessary revisions/updates. This side effect is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:19 applies discourse_expires_in 1.minute to a user-dependent TopicView response, so one user's rendering (e.g. staff-visible content) can be served to another from a proxy/CDN

ensure_embeddable hard-requires a Referer header, so embeds fail closed with InvalidAccess for legitimate visitors under Referrer-Policy: no-referrer or HTTPS→HTTP downgrade; only one host is supported and there is no scheme/port check (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26)

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, access is gated by `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, and it raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` when the referer host doesn't exactly match. If `request.referer` is missing (e.g., due to `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, some privacy tools, or browser referrer stripping), `URI('')` yields a `nil` host, which will not equal the configured host and will therefore always raise. This makes embeds fail closed for legitimate requests that simply lack a Referer header. The check also only supports a single configured host and compares only the host (no scheme/port), which matches the finding’s description.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:18-30 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' examples never stub feed_polling_enabled? to true, so they pass on the first guard clause and would still pass if the url/username checks were deleted; poll_feed itself has no coverage

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Jobs::PollFeed#execute`, `poll_feed` is only called when **all** three conditions are true: `feed_polling_enabled?`, `feed_polling_url.present?`, and `embed_by_username.present?`. In `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb`, the examples "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" only stub the URL/username to `nil` but do **not** stub `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` to `true`. Given the default in `config/site_settings.yml` is `feed_polling_enabled: false`, these specs can pass due to the first guard failing, and would still pass even if the URL/username checks were removed. Also, there are no specs exercising the `poll_feed` method behavior itself in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 replaces PostCreator.new(..., created_at:, category:) with TopicEmbed.import_remote, dropping the original topic timestamp and the --category option (removed at line 117) so imported threads are dated today and uncategorized; there is also no rescue around the network fetch so one dead link aborts the import

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the `--category` option entirely (`method_option :category` deleted) and deletes the logic that looked up `category_id`. It also replaces `PostCreator.new(..., created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id)` with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, and `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`.import` do not pass `created_at` or any category to `PostCreator`, so imported topics/posts will use the current timestamp and default category behavior. Additionally, `import_remote` calls `open(url).read` with no rescue in the task, so a fetch error for a single link can raise and abort the import run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20-22 defines feed_key computing a feed-modified: cache key that is never read or written, so the hourly job re-downloads and re-imports the whole feed every time while the dead method advertises caching that does not exist

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb a `feed_key` method is introduced that computes a Redis-style cache key (`"feed-modified:..."`), but the diff contains no code that ever calls `feed_key` or uses it to read/write any last-modified/etag state. The `poll_feed` method always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates `rss.items` on every run, so there is no caching/throttling based on `feed_key` as the method name/comments imply. While `TopicEmbed.import` is somewhat idempotent (checks existing embed/content_sha1), the job still re-downloads and re-processes the entire feed each hour and the `feed_key` method is dead/unreferenced.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:7,12 requires discourseUrl to end in '/' (undocumented) or the URL becomes http://example.comembed/best, and uses comments without a null check so a page missing #discourse-comments throws a TypeError

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, the iframe URL is built via string concatenation: `iframe.src = discourseUrl + "embed/best?..."`. If `discourseUrl` does not end with `/`, this produces `http://example.comembed/best...` (missing slash). Also, `comments` is assigned `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then used immediately as `comments.appendChild(iframe)` without checking for null, so pages that include the script but do not have an element with id `discourse-comments` will throw a TypeError.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:28 sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL, which is not a valid header value and is treated inconsistently by browsers; the header should be deleted or CSP frame-ancestors used instead

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, which sets `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:28). `X-Frame-Options` only standardly supports `DENY`, `SAMEORIGIN`, and the (deprecated) `ALLOW-FROM <uri>`; `ALLOWALL` is non-standard and is ignored/handled inconsistently by browsers. As a result, embedding may still be blocked (e.g., if a default `SAMEORIGIN` header is otherwise applied), so this is a real compatibility/correctness issue introduced by the diff.
